question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For compensation the bead set is the essential minimum.

With a biotinylated antibody panel on streptavidin capture beads you need one
compensation bead per fluorochrome that will be used on the sorter and one
unstained bead reference for autofluorescence / bead background.

* 1 x unstained / streptavidin-only beads
* 1 x AF350 streptavidin bead single stain
* 1 x GFP streptavidin bead single stain
* 1 x PE streptavidin bead single stain
* 1 x AF647 streptavidin bead single stain
* 1 x AF750 streptavidin bead single stain

That is n + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6 bead tubes for a correct spectral unmixing / 
compensation matrix. The unstained bead tube sets the bead autofluorescence
and the five single-stain tubes give the spillover values for AF350, GFP,
PE, AF647 and AF750 in the five detection channels.

In a real sort those compensation bead controls are necessary but not 
sufficient. In practice you will also run the biological system:

* Unstained cells/beads for cellular autofluorescence
* 5 Fluorescence Minus One FMOs for the 5 reporter gates, and typically a
positive and a viability control for the sort population.

That brings a routine 5-colour sort to 1 unstained cell + 5 single-stain
beads + 5 FMOs = 11 functional tubes in addition to the sample, with the
6 bead tubes above being the essential compensation minimum.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: For compensation the minimum, bead-based, set is n single colour standards + one negative bead/cell reference.

With 5 detection channels AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 you need

* 1 x unstained / bead-only / unstained cell negative control for autofluorescence and instrument background
* 5 x single fluorochrome Streptavidin-bead compensation standards, one per fluorochrome, i.e.

  AF350-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  GFP-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  PE-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  AF647-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  AF750-biotin capture on streptavidin beads

That is 5+1 = 6 essential compensation / instrument controls. The unstained bead control can be run as bead-only and as unstained cells, in practice one negative cell control and one negative bead control.

For a sorting experiment best practice is to add the gating controls. In addition to the 6 compensation controls you want an unstained cell control for gate placement and a Fluorescence Minus One control for each of the 5 markers to define a positive gate in the presence of the other 4 fluorochromes’ spillover. That is 1 unstained cell + 5 FMO = 6 cell-gating controls, 6 + 5 single-bead = 11 cell/bead controls in total, often quoted as n single stains + n FMOs + 1 unstained = 11 for n =5. The 5 single-bead standards are the essential streptavidin-bead compensation set.

that you will put on the cytometer.

and AF750.
* 5 x single-colour compensation bead tubes – one streptavidin-coupled

for each of the five detectors

same panel it is the  n + 1  rule, n = 5.

In practice a sorting experiment is run on cells, not on beads, so the bead

* 1 x unstained cell control for autofluorescence and spread/voltage setting;
* 5 x fluorescence minus one, FMO, cell controls, one per channel, for
unbiased placement of sort gates.

That is 1 unstained cell + 5 FMOs + the 5 single-stain bead compensation
tubes = 11 controls in total, 12 if a viability dye control is counted
separately, which is the conventional rigorous sorting panel for a 5-colour
streptavidin-biotin panel. The 6 bead tubes are the essential compensation
minimum from which the compensation matrix is built; the FMOs and the cell
unstained are the essential gating controls for a reliable sort.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum essential for compensation and basic gating is n fluorochromes + 1 negative.

For 5 detection channels AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 you need

* 1 unstained / autofluorescence negative control. With streptavidin beads this is unstained beads and/or unstained cells to set the negative boundary and to assess bead autofluorescence / non specific binding of streptavidin;
* 1 single colour compensation control per fluorochrome, made on the same matrix you will sort, i.e. streptavidin beads loaded with a bright sample of each streptavidin-fluorochrome conjugate: AF350-streptavidin, GFP-streptavidin, PE-streptavidin, AF647-streptavidin and AF750-streptavidin.

That is 5 single-stain compensation controls + 1 unstained negative = 6 essential controls. Those 6 are sufficient to generate an accurate compensation matrix and to set a basic negative gate.

In practice for a sort the recommended rigorous set is the 6 above plus fluorescence minus one gating controls. That is 5 FMO controls, one per channel, bringing the best-practice set to 1 unstained + 5 single-stain compensation + 5 FMO = 11 samples. The FMOs are not strictly required for compensation but they are essential for unambiguous multicolour gating in a sort where spill-over and dim populations matter.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum viable for compensation and negative gating is 1 + n fluorophores.

For a 5-fluorophore panel on streptavidin capture beads you need

* 1 negative / unstained bead control: streptavidin beads alone, no biotinylated fluorophore, in the same buffer as the stain. This sets autofluorescence / bead background and the baseline gate for sorting.
* 1 single-stain compensation control per fluorophore on streptavidin beads. The biotinylated fluorophore is captured on the streptavidin bead so that the bead is bright and essentially 100% positive in that channel and negative in the others. That is

  * AF350-biotin on streptavidin beads
  * GFP-biotin on streptavidin beads 
  * PE-biotin on streptavidin beads
  * AF647-biotin on streptavidin beads
  * AF750-biotin on streptavidin beads

5 single-color compensation controls + 1 unstained negative = 6 essential bead controls.

That is the minimal set that will allow you to calculate a 5 × 5 compensation matrix and define a negative population for each detector AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

In practice for a sorting experiment you want robust gate placement and you will normally add Fluorescence Minus One controls, one FMO per channel, i.e. 5 FMOs, on top of the 6 above. With FMOs the routinely used best-practice set is 1 unstained + 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 11 controls, the 6 compensation/negative controls being the strictly essential ones.
